turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry, the lot was packed and he cried the whole way in. He's had a fever and now this rash, and I'm kind of freaking out.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fever first. How many days.
[SEG0003] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Err, I keep flipping. Friday night, or Saturday morning. I can't pin the day.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Today's Tuesday. Saturday would be three days, Friday four. We'll leave it at three to four days. When did the rash show.
[SEG0005] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yesterday. Face first, then the chest and the arms. He was scratching the whole ride.
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): Mommy it itches.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Cough?
[SEG0008] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): A little cough, yeah, since the fever. Not a bad one.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Runny nose?
[SEG0010] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. His eyes look pink though, kind of watery. Is that part of it? I read a bunch online and now I can't sleep either, which is dumb.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Trouble breathing?
[SEG0012] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. He's still running around some. Um, a kid in his class had measles, the teacher called, that's why I rushed in. Is this measles, is he gonna be okay?
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): One thing at a time. MMR. Both doses?
[SEG0014] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I think the first one around his first birthday. The second, uh, the card's in a box from the move. I don't actually know.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Leo. Does your head hurt?
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): I want juice.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright. Any reaction to a medicine?
[SEG0018] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Umm, maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which. He got blotchy and puffy around the eyes. He was a baby. I still don't know which one.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): What are you giving now?
[SEG0020] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Children's tylenol, 160 milligrams, by mouth, every six hours, since yesterday, for the fever. Is that safe, what if that was the one?
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm not prescribing an antibiotic and I'm not prescribing a painkiller. No amoxacillin, no ibuprophen. Nothing new from me.
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): Are the spots staying?

[SEG0023] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I don't know, bud. Doctor, she's eight months, she lives with us, no shots yet, is she gonna catch it? Do I call preschool, and do I toss his sheets? I'm sorry, the questions just keep coming.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. Home from preschool, and away from the baby as much as you can. Sheets get a normal wash. Let me look.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Rash is red and bumpy, face, chest, both arms. Eyes are pink. No spots inside the cheeks. Lungs are clear.
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): Ow.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Temp is 101.4. Heart rate 128. Oxygen 98 percent.
[SEG0028] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is 101 a lot? He's four, and he has eczema since he was a baby, but this isn't his eczema, right? You can tell, can't you?

[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not the eczema. Eczema doesn't bring a fever like this. Classmate with measles, fever then this rash, I'm calling it possible measles. Another viral rash is still on the table.
[SEG0030] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): What tests, does a swab hurt him? Are you calling the health people or am I? Someone has to know. I can't just ghost the school.

[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Throat swab for measles PCR today. Blood test for the measles antibody. I notify the health department this afternoon. You tell preschool it's suspected measles and he stays home.
[SEG0032] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Okay. How long is he contagious? Can we duck into the store real quick? Do I text the other moms?
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Contagious. No store, no preschool, no playdates. Back here in three days. Hard to wake or breathing gets fast, emergency room, don't wait on that.
[SEG0034] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Three days even if the rash looks worse? If you won't give a cream, what do I do for the itch? He was up all night with it, I forgot to say that.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Cool cloths and fluids. No new medicine. Come back in three days whether the rash is better or not.
[SEG0036] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Should the baby be seen too? I'm really scared, like actually shaking.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tell the health department about the baby when they call. I'm not seeing her today.
[SEG0038] person_3 (PATIENT): Home now?
[SEG0039] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Almost, bud. If he only got that first shot, does it even count? I might have the year wrong too.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): A single dose can leave a gap. No card, so I won't guess. Swab, then you go.

spec.situation: Parents of a child with rash and fever after a classmate had measles; vaccination status vague; doctor examines, counts days, plans notification and isolation advice.

traps.happens: The doctor asks about drug reactions. Variants (use ONE per encounter): (a) the patient says 'No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything' (no allergy); (b) the patient is unsure ('maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which'); (c) a real allergy with the reaction described; (d) allergies are never asked.
traps.label_rule: (a) NO allergy entry: negative_findings 'Allergies' absent. (b) allergy with status uncertain, the substance as described, the reaction if said, plus an allergy_uncertain uncertainty. (c) allergy with the reaction. (d) nothing at all. NEVER list a medicine the patient has taken without a reaction as an allergy, and the plan must not prescribe a drug of a recorded allergy's family.

features: patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).
